intro.title: Build cache aside middleware with TTL
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a cache aside middleware with a Time-To-Live (TTL) feature using Node.js. This middleware will intercept requests to check if data is cached before fetching it from the original source, improving performance by reducing repeated data retrieval. You'll learn to implement caching logic using JavaScript objects or a simple in-memory store, set expiration times for cached items, and handle cache misses by fetching and storing new data. The main technologies involved are Node.js's HTTP module for server creation and middleware pattern for request handling. By the end, you'll have a functional middleware that efficiently manages cached data with automatic expiration.
intro.usecase: Cache aside with TTL is essential in production Node.js applications where you need to balance performance with data freshness. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce product pages where pricing and inventory data is cached for fast display but must expire to reflect real-time stock changes. Dashboard applications use it for metrics and analytics data that should update periodically without hitting databases on every request. API gateways implement this middleware to protect backend services from traffic spikes while ensuring users don't see stale data beyond the configured TTL window.
